title: Lease Expiry Is Close: A Practical Tenant Action Plan
excerpt: When lease expiry is approaching, focus on verified dates, business continuity, credible options and clear decision ownership.
author: Joe Kelley
metaTitle: Commercial Lease Expiry Action Plan | YOS
metaDescription: A practical action plan for business tenants approaching commercial lease expiry or renewal.
body:
A short runway reduces the time available to inspect alternatives, obtain advice and complete works. It does not mean you should make an uninformed decision.

## Confirm the dates and obligations

Check expiry, option notice dates, holding-over terms, make-good obligations and any notice requirements with a commercial property lawyer. Do not rely on memory or an informal summary.

## Set the business brief

Confirm whether the current premises still support the team, customers, operations, budget and future plans. Separate essential requirements from preferences.

## Open both pathways

Request a documented renewal proposal while testing credible alternatives. The aim is to create information and continuity options, not artificial pressure.

## Build a decision timetable

Assign owners and deadlines for inspections, cost comparison, legal review, technical checks, approvals and implementation. Make dependencies visible.

## Protect continuity

Consider what happens if documents, approvals, fitout or relocation take longer than planned. Record a contingency path.

Your Office Space can help organise the brief, alternatives and commercial comparison. Earlier is better, but a structured process still matters when time is limited.
